rounds.proof_sketch: Host uses elements_per_block=256 to compute num_blocks=65536. Kernel uses elements_per_block=257 for start_idx=bid*257. Block coverage: [b*257, b*257+256]. Ranges are contiguous (no gaps/overlaps). Last element 16,777,215 is in block 65280 (exists since 65536>65280). All elements processed exactly once regardless of value.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation only changes the internal loop organization within the kernel, not the host's block count calculation. With elements_per_block=257 in kernel and num_blocks computed from 256, each block processes a contiguous 257-element range with start_idx=bid*257. Since these ranges are perfectly contiguous and sufficient blocks are launched (because 256<257 means we always over-provision blocks), every output element is computed exactly once. The thread-to-element mapping changes, but the pooling computation per element is identical. No input values can expose this organizational difference.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable. The mutation alters internal work distribution but maintains complete, non-overlapping coverage of all output elements. The computation performed for each element is unchanged.
rounds.recommendations: When testing GPU kernel mutations involving work distribution constants (like elements_per_block), verify both that sufficient work units are launched AND that the coverage partitioning produces complete, non-overlapping element processing. Mutations to such constants are often equivalent if they only affect internal scheduling without changing the total coverage.
